title: AcmeDB 2.0: Finally, Backups
take: the boring database finally learned how to save your ass
screenshot_alt: acmedb doctor output: three green checks and one passive-aggressive yellow one
tldr: Snapshots exist now. Real ones: online, point-in-time, restorable without a support ticket. That was the dealbreaker in our last verdict and it is gone. The rest is one config rename, one protocol cut, and a health check with opinions.

breaking.fix: Rename the key in acmedb.toml. 2.0 refuses to boot on the old name instead of quietly ignoring it, which is rude but correct.

breaking.change: The v1 wire protocol is gone
breaking.fix: Drivers older than 1.8 can no longer connect. Bump the driver first, then the server. Not the other way round, unless you enjoy pages at 3am.

highlights.name: Point-in-time snapshots
highlights.what: acmedb snapshot create takes a consistent snapshot without pausing writes, and restore replays the WAL to any second inside the retention window. This is the feature we yelled about. It is real.
highlights.claim: Snapshots are online, incremental, and restorable to any point in the last seven days.

highlights.name: Manifest compaction
highlights.what: The manifest no longer grows forever, so cold starts on old databases drop from minutes to seconds. Nobody will tweet about it. Everybody will feel it.
highlights.claim: Cold start on a 500 GB database fell from 4 minutes to 9 seconds.

highlights.name: acmedb doctor
highlights.what: A health check that tells you what is wrong in plain English instead of a hex dump. Petty? Yes. Useful? Also yes.

preflight: Back up the AcmeDB data directory
Bump every client driver to 1.8 or newer
Check free disk space for the snapshot store
upgrade_steps: Rename wal_dir to storage.wal_path in acmedb.toml
Install AcmeDB 2.0 with the command below
Start AcmeDB and confirm acmedb doctor is green
rollback: Restore the pre-upgrade backup of the data directory
Reinstall the 1.9.x package and start it
known_issues: Snapshots of databases over 2 TB take hours, not minutes.
Still single-region. Cross-region replication is on the roadmap. Again.
bottom_line: This is the release that moves AcmeDB from cute toy to fine for prod, behind a cache. Upgrade, take a snapshot, go to bed.

notes.config: In 1.x the old key was silently ignored, which is how half of you ended up writing the WAL to /tmp.
notes.drivers: Driver 1.8 shipped in March. If you are older than that, the protocol cut is the least of your problems.
notes.retention: Seven days is the default. The changelog says it is configurable and does not say how far. We asked.
